issues.label: Subject-matter jurisdiction retained
issues.why: Court must confirm it retained jurisdiction after bifurcated decree to decide child support and property division.

issues.label: Finality and appealable orders
issues.why: Court must determine which orders are final and how post-trial motions affect finality and appellate timelines.

issues.label: Authority for bifurcated divorce
issues.why: Court must ensure bifurcation and reservation of issues were permissible and properly documented.

issues.label: Enforce stipulation reimbursement term
issues.why: Court must interpret and enforce the April 2022 stipulation for $61,690 repairs reimbursement and integrate it into property division.

issues.label: Scope of reserved issues
issues.why: Court must ensure it adjudicates all reserved matters (support and property) and does not exceed the reservation.

issues.label: Civil Rule 90.3 applicability
issues.why: Court must apply Alaska Civil Rule 90.3 correctly for pre-majority support and any permissible deviations.

issues.label: Support period end date
issues.why: Court must determine when the child support obligation ends (e.g., high school graduation) under Rule 90.3.

issues.label: Adult child support authority
issues.why: Court must identify the legal basis and limits for ordering post-majority support for a disabled adult child.

issues.label: Standard for disabled adult support
issues.why: Court must decide what findings are required (disability, dependency, necessity) to justify ongoing support.

issues.label: Custody prerequisite for support
issues.why: Court must address whether a support award requires a custodial parent when the child lives in an institution.

issues.label: Define primary physical custody
issues.why: Court must determine who had primary physical custody for Rule 90.3 purposes when neither parent housed the child.

issues.label: Institutional placement effect
issues.why: Court must evaluate how assisted living/state placement affects parental support obligations and custody analysis.

issues.label: Role of guardianship status
issues.why: Court must consider whether Duckett’s guardianship/conservatorship establishes custodial status or affects support entitlement.

issues.label: Past support calculation method
issues.why: Court must compute retroactive support correctly (start date, end date, monthly amounts) and explain the calculation.

issues.label: Retroactive support permissible scope
issues.why: Court must ensure any retroactive support award is authorized and limited by Alaska law and Rule 90.3.

issues.label: Income determination accuracy
issues.why: Court must make supported findings on Cline’s adjusted annual income and include required income components under Rule 90.3.

issues.label: Imputation vs actual income
issues.why: Court must decide whether to use actual earnings, earning capacity, or imputed income given job change and prospects.

issues.label: Effect of new employment
issues.why: Court must determine how Cline’s new pilot job and wage decrease affect current and future support.

issues.label: Treatment of irregular income
issues.why: Court must decide how to treat bonuses, variable pay, or non-wage income consistent with Rule 90.3.

issues.label: Deductible expenses and adjustments
issues.why: Court must ensure proper adjustments (taxes, mandatory retirement, health premiums, etc.) in calculating adjusted income.

issues.label: Support for child not in home
issues.why: Court must decide whether support should be paid to Duckett, to a trust, or directly for the child’s benefit.

issues.label: Allocation of extraordinary expenses
issues.why: Court must address how to allocate medical/therapy/special needs expenses beyond basic support, if applicable.

issues.label: State benefits interaction
issues.why: Court must evaluate how Medicaid/state payments and anticipated Social Security affect need and amount of support.

issues.label: Social Security timing contingency
issues.why: Court must craft enforceable terms for support ending or adjusting upon Social Security approval/receipt.

issues.label: Need-based findings for post-majority
issues.why: Court must support the $1,280/month necessity finding with evidence and specify what expenses are covered.

issues.label: Equal split rationale
issues.why: Court must justify splitting adult-child expenses 50/50 rather than using Rule 90.3 income-based proportions.

issues.label: Deviation from Rule 90.3
issues.why: If deviating from presumptive support, court must make required written findings and explain reasons.

issues.label: Support order clarity/enforceability
issues.why: Court must specify payment amount, frequency, payee, start date, termination, and modification triggers.

issues.label: Arrears computation and interest
issues.why: Court must determine arrears amount, whether interest accrues, and the applicable statutory rate.

issues.label: Modification standard preserved
issues.why: Court must ensure the order reflects standards for future modification (material change, Rule 90.3(h)).

issues.label: Credibility and evidentiary support
issues.why: Court must base support and expense findings on credible testimony and properly admitted evidence.

issues.label: Property division three-step test
issues.why: Court must apply Alaska’s classification-valuation-division framework for equitable distribution.

issues.label: Marital vs separate classification
issues.why: Court must determine whether the $100,000 mother transaction is separate inheritance, marital property, or mixed.

issues.label: Gift vs loan characterization
issues.why: Court must decide whether the mother’s $150,000 transfer was a true loan, a gift, or partly each.

issues.label: Debt forgiveness classification
issues.why: Court must classify the $50,000 loan forgiveness as marital benefit, separate gift, or both.

issues.label: Cash gift tracing
issues.why: Court must decide whether the $50,000 check can be traced as separate property after deposit into a joint account.

issues.label: Transmutation analysis
issues.why: Court must assess whether actions (joint deposit/use) showed intent to treat separate gift as marital.

issues.label: Commingling consequences
issues.why: Court must apply Alaska rules on commingling and whether funds became untraceable and thus marital.

issues.label: Donor intent relevance
issues.why: Court must weigh mother’s intent against recipient spouse’s intent and conduct in determining separateness.

issues.label: Burden of proof allocation
issues.why: Court must assign and apply the burden to prove separate property and traceability.

issues.label: Valuation date selection
issues.why: Court must choose and justify valuation dates for assets and debts (separation, trial, or decree) under Alaska law.

issues.label: Valuation of real property
issues.why: Court must determine fair market values of the marital real estate and address appraisal disputes.

issues.label: Treatment of trust-held proceeds
issues.why: Court must classify and allocate proceeds held in trust from sold marital properties and ensure proper accounting.

issues.label: Allocation of marital debts
issues.why: Court must identify, value, and allocate all marital debts, including any remaining obligations tied to properties.

issues.label: Scam loss characterization
issues.why: Court must decide whether Cline’s post-separation scam loss is marital waste, separate loss, or affects equity.

issues.label: Dissipation/waste findings
issues.why: If treating scam loss as dissipation, court must make findings on fault, intent, and impact on estate.

issues.label: Post-separation earnings treatment
issues.why: Court must determine how post-separation income and expenditures affect the marital estate and credits.

issues.label: Ramsey credit legal standard
issues.why: Court must apply the correct standard for awarding post-separation credits for preserving marital assets.

issues.label: Evidence for Ramsey credits
issues.why: Court must decide whether Cline proved amounts, necessity, and source of funds for claimed preservation expenses.

issues.label: Written findings on credits
issues.why: Court must make adequate findings to permit review when granting or denying claimed post-separation credits.

issues.label: Interaction with repair reimbursement
issues.why: Court must avoid double counting between the stipulated $61,690 reimbursement and claimed post-separation credits.

issues.label: Merrill factor application
issues.why: Court must consider and weigh Merrill factors (earning capacity, duration, conduct, etc.) in deciding an unequal split.

issues.label: Justification for 55/45 split
issues.why: Court must articulate why equity requires 55% to Duckett rather than equal division.

issues.label: Homemaker contribution weight
issues.why: Court must evaluate Duckett’s homemaker role and child-care responsibilities as contributions to the marital enterprise.

issues.label: Earning capacity comparison
issues.why: Court must make supported findings comparing future earning capacities and their impact on equitable division.

issues.label: Age and health considerations
issues.why: Court must consider parties’ ages/health including caregiving burdens that affect employability and needs.

issues.label: Economic circumstances post-divorce
issues.why: Court must assess each party’s financial condition after divorce, including housing and support responsibilities.

issues.label: Tax consequences relevance
issues.why: Court must consider tax impacts of property division where significant and reasonably certain.

issues.label: Capital gains tax allocation
issues.why: Court must determine how to allocate capital gains liabilities from sold marital assets and ensure consistent treatment.

issues.label: Mechanism to pay tax liability
issues.why: Court must decide whether trust funds should be used to pay taxes before distribution and issue enforceable directives.

issues.label: Timing and amount of tax
issues.why: Court must determine whether tax liabilities are fixed/known or contingent and how to handle estimates/true-ups.

issues.label: Debt vs expense classification of taxes
issues.why: Court must decide whether capital gains taxes are marital debts allocated in division or post-decree personal liabilities.

issues.label: Adequate findings requirement
issues.why: Court must issue sufficiently detailed findings on disputed material issues to allow meaningful appellate review.

issues.label: Reconsideration standard applied
issues.why: Court must apply the correct standard for reconsideration (new evidence, legal error, overlooked facts) and explain denial.

issues.label: Custody finding sufficiency
issues.why: On reconsideration, court must ensure its primary custody finding is explicit and supported by record evidence.

issues.label: Support recipient standing
issues.why: Court must ensure Duckett has standing to receive support payments for an adult child as guardian/conservator.

issues.label: Child support vs spousal support
issues.why: Court must ensure any payments ordered are properly categorized and not an impermissible substitute for spousal support.

issues.label: Consistency with stipulated terms
issues.why: Court must ensure final property division is consistent with prior stipulations unless modified with proper basis.

issues.label: Due process and notice
issues.why: Court must ensure both parties had notice and opportunity to litigate issues decided, including taxes and credits.

issues.label: Attorney’s fees consideration
issues.why: Court must consider whether to award need-based divorce attorney’s fees under Alaska law if requested/raised.

issues.label: Interest in trust administration
issues.why: Court must address how trust-held proceeds are administered, accounted for, and distributed consistent with decree.

issues.label: Allocation of ongoing child expenses
issues.why: Court must consider whether other children’s support obligations exist or were resolved and ensure no overlap/errors.

issues.label: Compliance with Rule 90.3 documentation
issues.why: Court must ensure required child support affidavits/worksheets and calculations are part of the record.

issues.label: Effective dates for obligations
issues.why: Court must specify effective dates for child support and any property equalization payments to prevent ambiguity.

issues.label: Offsetting payments and credits
issues.why: Court must determine whether any offsets apply between support arrears, reimbursements, and property equalization.

issues.label: Enforcement provisions
issues.why: Court must ensure orders are enforceable (withholding, payment routing, contempt standards) as appropriate.
